title: Generative AI Fundamentals
objective: Explain prompts, tokens, hallucinations, and RAG, and choose appropriate countermeasures for each use case.

sections.title: Plausibility Is Not a Guarantee of Accuracy
paragraphs: Generative AI generates text, images, code, and other content based on prompts. It can produce hallucinations—content that is plausible but factually incorrect—so for important decisions, design processes that verify outputs against approved sources and include human review.

sections.title: Communicating Goals and Constraints in Prompts
paragraphs: A prompt should clearly specify the subject, intended audience, output format, constraints, and information that may be referenced. Tokens are the units processed by the model, and the volume of input and output affects the context window, latency, and cost.

sections.title: Distinguishing single-generation, RAG, and AI agents by role
paragraphs: Single generation obtains a response from a single prompt. RAG retrieves documents relevant to a question, adds their content as context, and then generates a response. An AI agent plans toward a goal, uses authorized tools, checks intermediate results, and chooses its next action. When delegating external operations to an agent, design the scope of operations, required approvals, and execution records. Before deploying RAG, verify that the documents included in the search index are current and accurate. At retrieval time, limit results to documents the user can access, and evaluate whether the generated answer agrees with the cited sources. Use the diagram to locate the extra step for answering from documents and the human approval step before a consequential external action.

checkpoints.prompt: A member of the General Affairs Department wants to create a draft of the meeting minutes from a meeting transcript. Choose one method for turning the key points for each agenda item, decisions, and responsible people into written text based on the transcript and the specified format.

choices.text: Classify the meeting minutes by the type of past meeting.
choices.explanation: Classification selects a category. The classification result alone is not enough to create new meeting-minutes text from the input.

choices.text: Give the transcript and format to generative AI, and instruct it to mark any responsible person who is not mentioned as unconfirmed.
choices.explanation: Generative AI can create a draft based on the original text and format. Instruct it not to guess any responsible person who is not mentioned, and compare the draft with the original before publishing it.

choices.text: Use a regression model that predicts the end time from the meeting's start time.
choices.explanation: This process predicts a numerical value. It is not suitable for summarizing the key points for each agenda item or the responsible people in written form.

choices.text: Search past meeting minutes and save the single most similar one as is.
choices.explanation: Even if similar past material is found, it may not reflect the decisions or responsible people from this meeting.

checkpoints.prompt: A support lead at an online retailer uses generative AI to draft refund guidance for customers. To reduce errors in refund eligibility and amounts, choose one measure to take before sending the guidance to customers.

choices.text: Send it automatically without reviewing it.
choices.explanation: Even plausible-sounding output can contain errors.
This does not verify the accuracy of the content.

choices.text: Compare the draft with the approved refund conditions, and have the responsible employee review any guidance involving an exception or requiring a judgment before sending it.
choices.explanation: The amount and eligibility can be checked against the approved conditions. A person with authority to make refund decisions reviews how exceptions are handled.

choices.text: Have another generative AI summarize the draft, and send it as is if the summary has the same content.
choices.explanation: Even if the summary faithfully reflects the original draft, it does not verify whether the original eligibility and amount are correct. The draft must be compared with the approved refund conditions.

checkpoints.prompt: A product manager wants an answer for customers in three bullet points without speculation. What is the most direct way to specify this?

choices.text: Write constraints about the audience, format, and supporting evidence in the prompt.
choices.explanation: This makes the expected output easier to evaluate.
The requirements will not be conveyed.
This is not a substitute for conveying the constraints.

checkpoints.prompt: The head of the accounting department is introducing an AI agent that reviews invoices and creates payment requests. Which design is appropriate before payments are executed?

choices.explanation: There is no human control over a high-impact operation.

choices.text: Limit the tools the agent can use, require prior approval from an employee with payment authorization before executing a payment, and retain records of the approval and execution.
choices.explanation: Grant only the permissions needed to review invoices and create requests, while requiring an authorized employee to approve the execution of the transfer. The records can later be used to verify decisions and actions.

choices.text: Grant unlimited tool permissions as long as the plan is displayed.
choices.explanation: Displaying the plan alone does not prevent inappropriate execution.

choices.text: Skip approval because RAG is being used.
choices.explanation: Controls for retrieval and controls for external operations are separate.
